turn.user_message: What if some records are on paper?
turn.context: From transcript 20 (we bring this, this has to be there, and “if almost nothing is digital”) and bed-management.md §7.2 and §7.4.2.

transcript.label: After transcript turn 31 · Automations, turn 5 (the record stops at 31)

text: Some paper is fine. What we bring already reads from people, not from systems.
bullets: OPD advice is read from the prescription as written. Voice notes on rounds need no system at all.
Admissions, billing and the bed board are usually on a system already. Those need only read access.
If almost nothing is on a system, it is a different project, not a slower one. Better said now.
chat.invite: Tell me which of your records are still on paper.
prompts: What happens after the 6 PM freeze?
Which automation do we switch on first?
chat.pointer: Try the three settings, or flip the records yourself. The lamps show what still switches on.

blocks.title: Paper or system: what still works
blocks.deck: Each record is on a system or on paper. Each lamp lights only when everything it needs is on a system.

blocks.hint: Try a setting or flip a record. Pick a record to see what paper changes.

main.name: Discharge, automated
main.line: Built first, so its times are real

sources.name: OPD prescriptions
sources.holds: Read from the page as written, paper or not

sources.name: Voice notes on rounds
sources.holds: The doctor speaks. Our recorder writes the note

sources.name: Admissions and discharges
sources.holds: Who came in, who left, which bed, and when

sources.name: Bed board
sources.holds: Which beds are empty, being cleaned or ready

sources.name: Billing
sources.holds: When each bill closes and the next opens

sources.name: Inpatient notes
sources.holds: The stay so far, for each patient

blocks.condition: Paper notes do not stop the build. They make the part we bring bigger, and the timeline longer.

sheets.title: OPD prescriptions
sheets.text: The advice to admit is read from the prescription as written. Paper or screen makes no difference to this part.
sheets.entry: Are your OPD prescriptions written by hand?

sheets.title: Voice notes on rounds
sheets.text: The doctor speaks on the round they already do. Our recorder turns it into a note. No system is needed on the ward.
sheets.entry: Do your doctors write round notes by hand today?

hand.does: Speaks the note on the round.

sheets.title: Admissions and discharges
sheets.text: Almost every lamp needs this record. If it is kept in a register, we would have to build the record first.
sheets.entry: Is admission and discharge kept on a system or a register?

sheets.title: Bed board
sheets.text: Call-in times need to see which beds are ready. A whiteboard cannot be read by the engine.
sheets.entry: Is your bed board a system, a sheet or a whiteboard?

sheets.title: Billing
sheets.text: Billing is almost always on a system. The report joins bill close and bill open against the same bed.

lines.label: If on paper
lines.value: Dead bed time cannot be measured

sheets.entry: Is your billing on a system?

sheets.title: Inpatient notes
sheets.text: If these are on paper, voice notes on rounds can fill much of the gap. That is more for us to build.
sheets.entry: Which parts of the inpatient file are on paper?

blocks.label: Almost nothing on a system
blocks.sub: Not a slower one. The part we bring gets much bigger, and the timeline changes with it.
